We need to change the coordinate system from Cartesian coordinates to polar coordinates. To do this, we will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA={∬}_{Δ}\,f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,r\,dr\,d\theta .
$$

First, let's sketch our region $D:$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14141831/assets/f0a5627965f71f6eff869a45b1b575b892a67ebba9b1ec969f5dc38ba84cb250.png)

Notice that the region $D$ represents the disk of radius $3$ centered at $(0,-3).$ 

Cartesian and polar coordinates are connected by the following equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\ y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

With that in mind, let's now write the ${x}^{2}+(y+3)^{2}=9$ in polar coordinates:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+(y+3)^{2} & =9 \\ {(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )}^{2}+{(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +3)}^{2} & =9 \\ {r}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{r}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +6r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +9 & =9 \\ {r}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )+6r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =0 \\ {r}^{2}+6r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =0 \\ r(r+6\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since $r$ cannot be identical to zero on the entire circle, we must have $r=-6\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .$

Now, let's determine the limits for $r$ and $\theta .$ First of all, $r$ can vary from $r=0$ (at the origin) to $r=-6\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta $ (at the boundary of the region): 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14141831/assets/7515fffda1580baa332df454e7fe53a60f70944215f13d83e0e2269a0101dba6.png)

Secondly, $\theta $ can vary between $\theta =\pi $ (the negative $x$-axis) and $\theta =2\pi $ (the positive $x$-axis):

So, in polar coordinates $(r,\theta ),$ the region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(r,\theta )\,:\,0\le r\le -6\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\pi \le \theta \le 2\pi \}.
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}2xy\,\text{d}A & ={∬}_{Δ}2(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,r\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{-6\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }2{r}^{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{-6\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{r}^{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta .\end{aligned}
$$
